subject: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
Hello,

as far as i see all factor mean and covariance are fixed to 0,1 in default multiplegroup analysis, right?

Do i need to unconstrain them, when i don't assume that both might not be the same in all groups?

Best, Hans

messages.author: 70d0917afd869432
messages.subject: Re: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
Hi Hans,

The default is to have them fixed for identification purposes.

If you want to let them vary, you will have to constrain at least one slope and intercept across groups (at the bare minimum) in your model statement (more is better).

Then, in your multipleGroup() call add: invariance = c('free_cov','free_means')

Cheers,

Matt

messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: Re: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
Hi matthew, thanks for your response.

Maybe some context is helpful :D

I want to assess the magnitude of DIF between two groups. For the first group i have validated item parameters and i want to keep them fixed throughout the analysis. As a first step, i used the existing parameters to estimate theta. While group one has a mean of around 0, group two has a lower mean of -0.5.

I then used ordinal regression models to predict the response by theta and theta*group to see if group has an influence. In general, this influence seemed to be small.

To investigate the impact of correcting for DIF on theta, i thought i just release for every item (one at a time) the item parameters and reestimate them, just using group two. I did this with multipleGroups(), but i didn't release the GROUP mean/covariance for group two. I then found that the difference between the theta estimates of the original model and the model where i had the parameters unconstrained for one item was again quite small, when i used all items to estimate theta. I felt that this made perfect sense, because i released on out of 30 items and that shouldn't make too much of a difference.

However, today i checked the analysis again and i thought the mean is different between groups, so i probably should release it as well, but I am not sure whether this is a sensible thing to do. For example, the theta estimate for the people who answered to every item with 0 changes by about 0.3 thetas. It feels that now the released item somehow catches the mean difference? So, contrary to my prior analysis i have no relatively large differences in theta estimates between the original and the model with unconstrained parameters. Most of the difference is due to a large proportion of people answering all items with zero.

So, now i don't know which result is the "right" one. What are arguments to release/constrain the group-parameters?

Thanks a lot for any ideas!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
Hi Hans,

I see your point about wanting to keep one groups as a kind of population model based on previous results while freely estimating the second group parameters. It's not the typical DIF approach, but if you have a good reason to do it this way then I see no real harm.

The first step I would do in this situation is to set up a highly constrained model, where across all groups you set the parameters equal to the population values you have while freely estimating the latent mean and variance. If no DIF exists, this will provide an unbiased estimate of group differences. 

When testing DIF in this situation, it's perfectly fine to free the parameters in the second group only and test whether the log-likelihood significantly decreases via anova(), and simply loop over each item to run the tests. In fact, you could freely estimate *all* of the parameters in your focal group and compare the log-likelihood/information statistic (I would use information) drop to see if the included flexibility contributes to the overall model fit if you wanted to. If it does, DIF likely exists somewhere, and using item plots will help to see what exactly is happening. 

It's too bad you want to treat your reference group as a population model, since there is a new DIF function specifically for running these kinds of analyses when multiple group samples are drawn. Could have made the looping a little easier, IMO. Cheers.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
Dear Phil,

when i set all item parameters to be equal in both groups to the population values and allow only GROUP mean/covariance to be estimated (i do this in the parameter-table), mirt gives nonetheless mean = 0, cov = 1 for both groups?

The means of the estimated thetas differ, though.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
Indeed, that looks to have been a break early bug since the EM wasn't quite set up to run with only group parameters estimated. Fixed and updated on Github. The following code now works:

````
set.seed(12345)
a <- matrix(abs(rnorm(15,1,.3)), ncol=1)
d <- matrix(rnorm(15,0,.7),ncol=1)
itemtype <- rep('dich', nrow(a))
N <- 1000
dataset1 <- simdata(a, d, N, itemtype)
dataset2 <- simdata(a, d, N, itemtype, mu = .1, sigma = matrix(1.5))
dat <- rbind(dataset1, dataset2)
group <- c(rep('D1', N), rep('D2', N))
models <- mirt.model('F1 = 1-15')

sv <- multipleGroup(dat, models, group = group, pars = 'values') 
sv$est <- FALSE
sv$est[123:124] <- TRUE #free only means and var for group 2
mod <- multipleGroup(dat, 1, group, pars = sv)
coef(mod)[[2]]$GroupPars
    MEAN_1 COV_11
par  0.043  1.968
````
Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
On Mon, Dec 16, 2013 at 2:54 PM, <bea...@gmx.de> wrote:
Thanks Phil, now it's working. When you say "In fact, you could freely estimate *all* of the parameters in your focal group and compare the log-likelihood/information statistic (I would use information) drop to see if the included flexibility contributes to the overall model fit if you wanted to." you mean to still constrain the factor means/covariation, right?

Correct, the model will still be identified (up to two parameters have to remain fixed actually for identification, but the rest are fair game). 

As it turns out though if you are only keeping the reference group in with fixed parameters and latent N(0,1) distribution then you actually can do this without MG analysis at all. Since there are no equality constraints across groups, and the reference group never changes, the log-likelihoods across groups are strictly additive and therefore the non-estimated groups just serve to add a constant to the likelihood. Inference wouldn't change since strictly independent groups provide no additional information about the focal (sample, in this case) group. The multipleGroup function is really only good when you have two samples to compare, not in the case where you are comparing how one sample matches with population coefficients. Sorry for not recognizing that earlier. 

Just set up your tests with a single group run using only your sample with the population coefficients you know, and perform likelihood-ratio tests on the less restricted versions of this model. If you are still interested in the latent mean and variance then try to set a slope coefficient to 1 and intercept parameter to 0 (match it with the population, as close as possible) so that the model is identified when these parameters are estimated.

The results seem now quite similar to my first run, when i had mean/cov fixed to 0/1 in both groups.

I really appreciate your quick help; mirt is one of my favourite packages and i learned a lot about IRT by using it in the past year. Keep up the good work!

Thanks for the kind words, I'm just glad to see this project getting good use, and your reports have certainly been helpful (and I'm sure the community appreciates it as well). Cheers.

Phil

dear phil,

is estimating item parameters with fixed latent variable mean/variance comparable to estimating a model in each sample independently and transforming item parameters using stocking-lord procedure?

thanks!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: release mean/cov in multiple group analysis
parts:
Yes, this is how the Stocking-Lord procedure is set-up. As it turns
out, the 'configural invariance' model in multiple group methodology
is formally equivalent to fitting independent single groups, so you
could just set up the model that way and use the patched version of
read.mirt(). Otherwise you could do this manually by setting up
individual single group models and going from there. Cheers.

Phil
